attribution_counterfactual.method: Counterfactual QED attribution. For each of the 8 ADS descriptors, replace ONLY that descriptor in every generated molecule with the real-cohort mean, recompute QED as the weighted geometric mean of the 8 ADS desirabilities (Bickerton 2012, WEIGHT_MEAN), and report the mean change.
attribution_counterfactual.validation: the reimplementation reproduces RDKit QED.qed to 1e-16 (0.094443 vs 0.094443)
attribution_counterfactual.reading: ROTB +0.057715 and ALERTS +0.056093 together account for 0.113808 of a 0.14034 gap. ALOGP +0.021093 is third. AROM is NEGATIVE (-0.02146): pushing aromatic-ring count to the real mean would make QED WORSE, so 'generate more aromatics' is not by itself a fix -- the ring has to be the right ring.
attribution_counterfactual.note: the counterfactual is a swap on a DESCRIPTOR, not on chemistry. It says which axis carries the gap, not which intervention works.

underlying_chemistry.reading: generated ligands are long, acyclic, triple-bond-rich and essentially non-aromatic. Real organometallic ligands are aromatic and compact. That single structural fact produces the ROTB gap, the ALERTS gap (the C#C structural alert alone fires on 67% of generated molecules) and most of the ALOGP gap (real logP 4.153034 vs generated 8.087648).

gap_in_its_own_units.sign_convention: generated_minus_real is negative: the generated cohort sits BELOW the real corpus by 0.14034 QED units, and reaches 40.225716% of the real value.

closest_published_value.note: These are the provenance of the FORMULAS. No published ADMET DISTRIBUTION for CFM-generated Pt/Ru anticancer complexes exists, so there is no external target to move toward -- only the real-cohort band, which is the honest reference.

ames_mutagen.reading: generated is 0 on all 66; real is 0.0349. Generated looks BETTER, and that is not a virtue -- it means the alert SMARTS never fire, which is a symptom of acyclic non-aromatic ligands, not of safety.

cell_permeability_logPapp.reading: generated -3.039 vs real -3.680: generated is 0.64 log units HIGHER (better). BUT the generated sd is only 0.143526 against a real sd of 1.0089, and the model output is pinned at the clipping boundary: the formula clips to [-8,-3] and the generated median is exactly -3.0. The generated distribution is a ceiling artefact, not a prediction.

aqueous_solubility_logS.reading: generated -8.010 vs real -6.701: generated is 1.31 log units WORSE. This is the one genuine ADMET failure, and it is fully explained by logP 8.087648 vs 4.153034 (ESOL's logP coefficient is -0.63) and RotB 16.863636 vs 5.176148 (+0.066 each).

the_structural_fact.evidence: molmetal/molmetal_lam/sbdd_env/metrics_v2.py -- ames_mutagen is 6 SMARTS matches; cell_permeability_logPapp is -4.0 + 0.33*logP - 0.013*TPSA + 0.40*HBD; aqueous_solubility_logS is 0.16 - 0.63*logP - 0.0062*MW + 0.066*RotB - 0.74*aromfrac. Every input is an ORGANIC descriptor.
the_structural_fact.consequence: ADMET cannot be a target objective on its own. It is a readout of organic-bulk realism. Any loss term that moves ADMET is, mechanically, a loss term that moves logP / RotB / aromaticity -- i.e. it is the QED lever again wearing a different hat.

the_zero_platinum_finding.measurement: Across THREE independent generated cohorts totalling 149 molecules (66 + 40 + 43), the metal counts are Ir 18, Ru 16, Rh 15, Re 13, Os 4 and Pt ZERO.
the_zero_platinum_finding.real_rate: Pt is 25.2% of the real six-metal corpus (7853 of 31150).
the_zero_platinum_finding.root_cause: NOT a model defect. It is a template-window sampling artefact: load_tmqm_clouds(n_clouds=192, seed=0, split='val') draws only the first 192 of 960 candidate val clouds, and that window contains Ru 64, Ir 45, Re 38, Rh 35, Os 10 and NO Pt. At n_clouds=960 there are 64 Pt; at n_clouds=2000 there are 491.
the_zero_platinum_finding.consequence: Every precious-metal-anticancer claim in this project is currently unmeasurable, because the generator is never asked for a platinum. The cheapest possible fix is to widen the template window, and it requires NO retraining and NO code change to the model -- only the sampling call. This is the highest-value, lowest-cost item in the whole inventory.
the_zero_platinum_finding.tag: MEASURED (counts) / the causal attribution to the sampling window is an inference from the n_clouds sweep, stated as such.
the_zero_platinum_finding.verdict_2026_10_12_A_vs_B: (A) SAMPLING ARTEFACT HOLDS; (B) retrain-on-window-with-Pt is REFUTED. Refuting evidence: the seed=0 TRAINING split (n_clouds=26715) contains 6634 Pt atoms (24.83% of atoms, SECOND-largest single-metal count behind Ru=7805/29.22%), so the checkpoint has seen Pt extensively. The val window of 192 (a reservoir sample of 960 candidates) happens to contain 0 Pt purely by reservoir luck. The val full pool (6714) has 1641 Pt (24.5%). Train and val-full agree at ~25% Pt; the 192-window reservoir does not. This is exactly the (A) signature -- the model is fine, the window is unlucky. CORRECTION APPENDED 2026-10-12: prior text said 'LARGEST single-metal count' for Pt, which is wrong -- Ru is the largest; load-bearing point (Pt is ~25%, the model has seen Pt extensively) survives.

the_zero_platinum_finding.patch_2026_10_12: Patched load_tmqm_clouds in molmetal/data/tmqm_clouds.py with a new keyword min_per_metal: int = 0. When min_per_metal >= 1 the loader back-fills reservoir slots so EVERY requested metal is represented at least that many times, by re-scanning the geometry shards. min_per_metal=0 is byte-identical to the original behaviour.

patch_verification.guard: min_per_metal=5 with n_clouds=10 raises ValueError('min_per_metal=5 * 6 = 30 exceeds n_clouds=10'). No silent truncation.
patch_verification.critical_fix: tmQM file atom order is arbitrary -- the metal is not always atomic_numbers[0]. The patch scans all atomic numbers for any metal Z, then picks the corresponding symbol. This is what makes the patch's own Pt count non-zero (the original naive zs[0] lookup found Pt=0 even when Pt was in the cloud).

On the PATCHED loader all 4 pass (kwarg accepted, Pt>=1 with min_per_metal=1, default behaviour pinned, underflow raises). After reverting min_per_metal from the signature all 4 FAIL with 'TypeError: load_tmqm_clouds() got an unexpected keyword argument min_per_metal' -- that is the red check the harness required.

decomposition_raw_scale.conversion: dSA = -(dRaw)/6.5*9 = -1.3846*dRaw. Sub-terms below are on the RAW sascorer scale, higher = harder.

fragment_rarity_term.reading: NEGATIVE dSA -- generated fragments are actually EASIER than real by this term. Fragment rarity is NOT the problem.

chiral_centre_penalty.reading: log10(nPotentialCentres+1). THIS IS THE SINGLE LARGEST COMPONENT OF THE ENTIRE SA GAP.
chiral_centre_penalty.sign_convention: negative d_sa_units = this term makes molecules HARDER to synthesise; the share is the magnitude

size_penalty.reading: molecule size differs by 0.012 SA units. Generated molecules are NOT too big.

macrocycle.reading: no generated molecule has a macrocycle; 1.1% of real ones do.

control_1_is_the_chiral_penalty_real.reading: The obvious objection is 'CSD just does not record stereo, so real molecules would look the same'. It does not survive: real tmQM has 0.201 POTENTIAL (unassigned) centres per molecule -- 0.201 -- versus 6.257576 for generated, a 31x difference. 89% of real molecules have ZERO potential stereocentres; only 97% of generated ones do. Excluding metal-adjacent centres (where an achiral coordination geometry is expected) still leaves 4.666667 vs 0.1805. The discrepancy is in the organic ligand, not at the metal.
control_1_is_the_chiral_penalty_real.control_that_WAS_vacuous: Chem.RemoveStereochemistry on the real corpus changes nothing, because sascorer counts POTENTIAL centres (includeUnassigned=True) and RemoveStereochemistry only clears stereo ANNOTATIONS. That control was run and reported identical numbers; it cannot discriminate and should not be cited.

control_2_is_this_fragment_library_bias.reading: generated fragments are BETTER covered by the PubChem rarity table than real ones (26.1% vs 21.9% missing). So the SA gap cannot be blamed on the model inventing exotic fragments.

gap_in_its_own_units.verdict: The SA gap is 1.464219 SA units and it is NOT what the repo has assumed. It is not fragment rarity (that term points the WRONG WAY, -0.32 SA units) and it is not molecule size (0.01 SA units). 71.6% of it is the stereocentre penalty, and the stereocentre count is a symptom of long acyclic sp3 ligand backbones -- the SAME structural defect that produces the QED ROTB and ALERTS gaps. SA and QED are one problem, not two.

the_decisive_structural_fact.evidence: Inside train_one_epoch, the counts are _bridge_components 0, _assemble_mol 0, generate_clouds_from_noise 1 (a comment, line 3409), Chem.MolFromSmiles 1 (the 4-SMILES PLL smoke at line 3176), QED 0. the_four_that_were_removed.why_the_sa_one_died: sa_loss was torch.tensor(float(_sa_pen.mean())) built from _synthesize_sa_scores_from_clouds(batch_clouds) -- a scalar constant detached from the graph, so it had no gradient path to any parameter. It was in the sum and contributing a number that looked like a loss and was not one.
the_four_that_were_removed.note: There is currently NO SA term and NO QED term in the loss. The user's stated goal of 'changing the loss to get better QED/SA/ADMET' has no existing implementation to tune -- it would have to be built, and the build has to start with making a decoded molecule.

verdict_per_target.QED: REACHABLE, but not by adding a QED term. The gap decomposes cleanly and ROTB (+0.0577) plus ALERTS (+0.0561) carry essentially all of it; both are consequences of one structural fact -- generated ligands are long, acyclic, triple-bond-rich and 98.5% non-aromatic (aromatic bond fraction 0.0012 vs real 0.4546). The lever that exists and is already live is bond_ce, i.e. bond-TYPE prediction, and it is currently LOSING: macro-F1(TYPE) 0.4784 +/- 0.0055 against OpenBabel's 0.5051 under the identical per-complex protocol (metrics/by_metric/tmqm_bond_perception_3seed.json). Fix bond-type accuracy and QED follows as a by-product. A black-box QED penalty is the wrong instrument and the BLK-C-L3 objection to it already stands.
verdict_per_target.ADMET: NOT A LOSS PROBLEM. Honest-negative, and here is why. All three implemented proxies are pure functions of logP, MW, TPSA, RotB, HBD and six SMARTS alerts -- not one of them reads the metal, so they cannot express anything metal-specific and cannot distinguish a cisplatin from a ruthenium dye. Measured against the REAL band instead of the circular decoder band, ames (0.0 vs 0.0349) and logPapp (-3.039 vs -3.680) are already better than real, and the logPapp 'win' is a clipping artefact (median pinned at -3.0, sd 0.14). Only logS is genuinely worse (-8.010 vs -6.701, by 1.31 log units) and that is entirely inherited from logP 8.09 vs 4.15. So the ADMET target reduces to the QED target. Build the three missing proxies (hERG, hepatotox, plasma binding) if you want an axis that discriminates; do not add an ADMET loss term.
verdict_per_target.SA: REACHABLE, and the repo's diagnosis of WHY is wrong. The 1.464219-unit gap is not fragment rarity -- that term points the wrong way (-0.32 SA units, and generated Morgan fragments are BETTER covered than real, 26.1% vs 21.9% missing from the PubChem rarity table). It is not molecule size (0.01 units). It is the stereocentre penalty: 71.6% of the gap, from 6.257576 potential stereocentres per generated molecule against 0.201 for real tmQM, and that survives excluding metal-adjacent centres. So SA and QED are ONE problem -- long acyclic sp3 ligand backbones -- and the same bond-type lever moves both. A fragment-rarity term would be aimed at a term that is already helping us.
verdict_per_target.precious_metal_anticancer_specific: MOST REACHABLE, LEAST MEASURED, AND CURRENTLY BLOCKED BY A SAMPLING ARTEFACT RATHER THAN BY THE MODEL. Geometry responds: guidance closes min_pair_distance from 0.602 to 0.017 absolute error with no retraining (metrics/by_metric/cfm_l3_guidance_ab.json), and metal_ligand_min has 0.351 Angstrom still open. But coordination number is NOT at parity as cfm_todo.json claims -- 4.879 generated vs 5.952 real, and the '4.91' in cfm_todo.json is the mean degree of the FAILING generated subset, mislabelled as real, so the gap is -1.074 coordination numbers rather than parity. Worse: the generated cohort contains ZERO platinum across 149 molecules in three independent cohorts, because load_tmqm_clouds(n_clouds=192) samples a 192-of-960 window that happens to contain no Pt, while Pt is 25.2% of the real six-metal corpus. Every anticancer-specific claim is unmeasurable until that window is widened -- which costs nothing and needs no retraining. And the metric that actually distinguishes a drug from a dye here, square-planar vs tetrahedral discrimination at Pt(II) (CShM SP-4 / tau-4'), is not implemented at all, while the project's own MetalCytoToxDB has zero Pt rows. So: not primarily a loss question. A data-sampling question first, a missing-metric question second, a loss question third.
